metric.why: PPAs are how the boom finances new generation and how operators back renewable claims. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular commitments, became the signature deals of the AI era.
metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are the financial mechanism by which AI operators lock in generation capacity years ahead, making them the primary signal of which technologies grid operators expect to build.

PPAs transfer the revenue risk of building new power plants from utilities to data center operators. When an operator signs a long-term contract for nuclear, solar, wind, or gas output, it guarantees the builder will recoup its capital cost. This matters for AI because the scale and timing of new generation directly constrains how many chips can run. Nuclear agreements became the defining deal type of the AI era because operators need baseload power that matches the always-on demand of compute clusters.

The pattern visible in PPA volume shows what generation technologies investors believe will actually get built. This is not the same as stated grid decarbonization goals. It is not the same as announced projects. It is the bet-with-money signal. Behind that signal sits the binding constraint: whether new plants will physically exist when data centers need power.

This data does not measure how much power was actually delivered, how many megawatts are operating today, or whether signed agreements will be completed. It does not isolate which operators signed which deals. It measures the mechanism itself, not its outcome.
